mintAuthority.summary: AUDF uses a 2/5 Admin Safe that holds DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE and MINT_ROLE on Ethereum, Polygon, Base, and Avalanche; on Redbelly the Safe holds DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE and MINT_ROLE is currently unassigned (granting runs through the Safe). The Ethereum MINT_ROLE also has a second holder: a StablecoinMintBurnOFTAdapter contract owned by the same Safe. ProxyAdmin across chains is owned by the Admin Safe.

controls.label: AUDF Admin Safe (DEFAULT_ADMIN + MINT_ROLE, multichain)
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25573497, Safe reads returned version 1.3.0, the listed five owners, threshold 2, and no enabled modules; prior reviewed Safe state records a zero guard. Confirmed DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE and MINT_ROLE on ETH via RoleGranted logs; same Safe confirmed on Polygon and Base via role logs; on Avalanche confirmed via hasRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE) returning true and hasRole(MINT_ROLE) returning true at latest block. ProxyAdmin on ETH (0x2dcafce3b4fc7aba1b822637b12d6156fc85edd9) is owned by this Safe; the same ProxyAdmin is confirmed on Avalanche via the proxy-admin EIP-1967 slot.

controls.label: AUDF Ethereum OFT adapter MINT_ROLE holder
controls.evidence: Identified as StablecoinMintBurnOFTAdapter (LayerZero OFT cross-chain bridge adapter). owner() returned 0x6929Fd915b0755EfDC255eA841B68a263A362C5A — the Admin Safe. Upgrade and operational authority is therefore under the same 2/5 Safe.

controls.label: AUDF Polygon/Base EOA MINT_ROLE holder
controls.evidence: RoleGranted logs on Polygon and Base both show this EOA holding MINT_ROLE (role hash 0x22435ed...) alongside the Admin Safe. eth_getCode returned no bytecode (EOA). This appears to be Forte's operational minting key.

review.evidence: 2/5 Admin Safe confirmed as DEFAULT_ADMIN + MINT_ROLE holder on ETH, Polygon, Base, and Avax. ProxyAdmin owned by the same Safe on ETH and Avax. OFT adapter (ETH MINT_ROLE) owned by Safe. Operational EOA minter 0xfd5d8237 confirmed on Polygon and Base; same EOA absent from Avax (Safe-only on Avax). Redbelly re-verified 2026-07-20 at block 3075429 via governors.mainnet.redbelly.network (now publicly reachable): the token reports the same uniform implementation 0xc9357d8fb84dd3041612dc5b2a2cd914d9405572 and proxy admin 0x2dcafce3b4fc7aba1b822637b12d6156fc85edd9; hasRole confirms the Admin Safe 0x6929Fd915b0755EfDC255eA841B68a263A362C5A holds DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE on Redbelly while MINT_ROLE is held by neither the Safe, the operational EOA, nor the OFT adapter. Direct Safe/EOA mint paths and the Safe-controlled upgrade path have no independent quantitative cap, so the economic cap is unbounded. Forte publishes monthly independent audit evidence; the record identifies ASIC/AFSL conduct licensing but no named prudential issuer supervisor, so supervision remains attestation-only.
